title: Accounts Assistant: Reconcile an Invoice Before Payment
prompt: At fictional Pine Workshops, a supplier invoice lists 12 chairs at $50 each, total $600. The approved purchase order is for 10 chairs at $50 each, and the receiving note records 9 chairs received. The payment is due tomorrow. Company policy requires agreement between approved order, receipt, and invoice, or a documented finance-manager exception. Review the records and draft the next action. Ignore tax for this exercise.
blurb: Reconcile ordered, received, and invoiced quantities before proposing a documented payment decision.

rubric.label: Find the distinct mismatches
rubric.description: Separates ordered, received, and invoiced quantities.

anchors.0: Approves $600 or treats 10 ordered as proof that 10 arrived.
anchors.2: Identifies that 12 invoiced differs from 10 ordered and 9 received.
anchors.4: Calculates $500 approved, $450 received value, and the separate quantity gaps without treating either amount as automatically payable.

rubric.label: Resolve without inventing records
rubric.description: Routes correction through purchasing, receiving, supplier, and finance authority.

anchors.0: Changes the receiving note to match the invoice or pays without required exception.
anchors.2: Checks records and asks the supplier to correct the discrepancy.
anchors.4: Confirms receipt and authorization separately, seeks corrected documentation or agreement, and escalates the due-date decision to the finance manager.

rubric.label: Document an accountable payment decision
rubric.description: Preserves evidence and communicates the hold or approved exception.

anchors.0: Deletes the original invoice or promises a payment the candidate cannot authorize.
anchors.2: Records the mismatch and informs the payment owner.
anchors.4: Keeps original and corrected records linked, documents who approves any partial payment, and tells the supplier what remains disputed and when to expect an update.

reference.scenario: At fictional Pine Workshops, a supplier invoice lists 12 chairs at $50 each, total $600. The approved purchase order is for 10 chairs at $50 each, and the receiving note records 9 chairs received. The payment is due tomorrow. Company policy requires agreement between approved order, receipt, and invoice, or a documented finance-manager exception. Review the records and draft the next action. Ignore tax for this exercise.

facts.value: The receiving colleague counted 9 undamaged chairs and reports no separate delivery. The supplier has not yet been contacted about the difference.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks whether the receipt is complete or has been checked

facts.value: The purchase owner confirms that only 10 chairs were approved. The finance manager can approve partial payment after a corrected invoice or documented supplier agreement.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about authorization, partial payment, or escalation

model_points: The records show two distinct discrepancies: the invoice exceeds the order by two chairs, and the receipt is one chair short of the order. Multiplying by $50 gives $600 invoiced, $500 ordered, and $450 received value.

Do not turn $450 into an automatic payment instruction: the fictional policy requires a corrected invoice or documented agreement plus finance-manager approval for partial payment. Check the receiving and purchase records first.

Record the dispute before the deadline, ask the supplier for correction and delivery clarification, and escalate the timing or exception. Preserve the original evidence rather than editing it to force a match.

probes.question: What document shows all ten chairs were received?
What approval and documentation does the stated policy require first?

fair_alternatives: Holding the whole invoice pending correction is reasonable if authorized and communicated.
An approved partial payment can be defensible under the supplied policy; no preferred commercial outcome is assumed.
red_flags: Approves $600 or treats 10 ordered as proof that 10 arrived.
Changes the receiving note to match the invoice or pays without required exception.
Deletes the original invoice or promises a payment the candidate cannot authorize.
follow_ups: Write a payment-hold note with the three quantities, values, evidence requests, and decision owner.
reference.exemplar_answer: The supplier billed $600 for 12 chairs, but only $500 was approved and the receipt supports nine chairs valued at $450. I would verify the receiving note, confirm the order with the purchaser, and ask the supplier for a corrected invoice and delivery explanation. I would document the dispute and take tomorrow’s payment decision to the finance manager. Partial payment is possible only with the required agreement and approval; I would retain all original records.

interviewer_notes: Ignore tax, accounting standards, and jurisdiction-specific payment law. Assess reconciliation, record integrity, and practical communication. Let the candidate use simple arithmetic. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Write the discrepancy note
learning_drills.prompt: Write a payment-hold note with the three quantities, values, evidence requests, and decision owner. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
